declared_proposition: Let H be a real symmetric finite Galerkin form, let B have full row rank, and let the columns of U span ker(B). Then H is nonnegative on the constraint core ker(B) if and only if the compressed form U^T H U is positive semidefinite. Positive ambient trace, positive ambient determinant, and a positive value on the all-ones vector do not imply this condition: H=diag(3,-1,-1), B=(1,1,1) has all three scalar diagnostics positive but the core witness (0,-1,1) has quadratic value -2.
mathematical_argument: Every constrained vector is Uc, so its quadratic value is exactly c^T(U^T H U)c; this proves the compression equivalence by congruence. For the displayed form, the kernel basis columns (1,-1,0) and (1,0,-1) give compressed matrix [[2,3],[3,2]], whose determinant is -5. The scalable diagonal family with two negative coordinates keeps trace, determinant, and the all-ones value positive while the sum-zero difference of the last two coordinates always has value -2.

discarded_route: scalar cancellation diagnostics such as trace, determinant, or one test-vector value as substitutes for constrained positivity
remaining_gap: The compression theorem is finite linear algebra. No uniform lower bound is proved for the actual Guinand-Weil matrices, and no cutoff-free positivity statement follows.
claim_boundary: No RH proof and no zero exclusion; exact finite compression criterion and scalable scalar-diagnostic no-go.
